Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=-4+5y-{y}^{2}$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4+5y-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-5y+4 & =0 \\ (y-1)(y-4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=1,\,4.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=1$ to $y=4.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{4}y(-4+5y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
